input: The wall thickness of the compressor casing is set by the pressure boundary and the corrosion allowance taken together, and with the allowance added the thickness works out at 22 mm. This figure is the finished wall, rather than the pressure-only thickness. The allowance is progressively consumed over the life of the unit, so the wall that resists $\Delta P$ at the end of that life is thinner than the wall that leaves the shop, and the stated 22 mm is the value that keeps the end-of-life wall at the required strength. The same casing carries the flanged joints at the suction and discharge nozzles, and at those joints the gasket choice is between two materials that differ, for the purposes of this report, only in temperature limit. The higher-rated material is preferred. The discharge end of the casing runs hotter than the suction end, the margin between the metal temperature and the lower rating is the margin the joint tightens against as the unit heats, and a gasket that is adequate at the suction flange is not thereby adequate at the discharge flange.
